identity.scope: The accepted COL26.8 nomenclatural usage is Cercopithecus diana (Linnaeus, 1758). The biological article studies the Diana monkey subspecies C. d. diana and its sampled wild populations; it is not used to establish COL identity or full species-concept circumscription.

systematicSearch.scope: Exact COL26.8 identity and full parent chain; targeted review of one primary playback study with item-level license evidence.
systematicSearch.method: Resolved the COL usage and each parent by stable ID in the release-pinned search and hierarchy registry. Reviewed the article abstract, methods, results, discussion, item-level XML license notice, and associated metadata. This is not a systematic search across the biological literature or facet-specific databases.
systematicSearch.queryOrPath: Pinned COL26.8 dataset 316115 usage 5XKC5; Europe PMC PMCID PMC4785987; DOI 10.1098/rsos.150639.
systematicSearch.inclusionCriteria: Exact accepted COL identity and statements explicitly reported for Diana monkey callers, receivers, study sites, and playback conditions in the cited primary paper.
systematicSearch.exclusionCriteria: Name-only joins; claims about other species; range-wide extrapolation from two study populations; claims about unstudied behaviors or conditions; unassessed morphology, reproduction, phylogeny, fossil record, distribution, and conservation facets.

gaps: The selected playback study does not assess anatomical morphology or diagnostic characters.

claims.text: The playback study tested whether male Diana monkeys distinguished familiar from unfamiliar male callers during responses to predator-specific alarm calls at Taï Forest and Tiwai Island. At both sites, acoustic features of responses varied with caller familiarity, but the direction of the familiar-versus-unfamiliar pattern differed between sites. The authors also report that familiarity affected leopard-induced alarms at Taï but not at Tiwai.
claims.locator: Abstract; Material and methods > Subjects and playback stimuli, paragraph beginning ‘We tested different groups of Diana monkeys’; Results > Call-related parameters, paragraph beginning ‘To eagle alarm calls, responses showed frequency transitions’; Discussion
claims.placeTimeScope: Wild Diana monkeys at Taï Forest, Côte d’Ivoire (N=20, August to December 2013), and Tiwai Island, Sierra Leone (N=23, January to March 2014); playback observations and conclusions are restricted to these two study populations.
claims.lifeStatus: Wild adult male Diana monkeys and their alarm-call responses; no captive or domesticated animals are included. The study does not assess development, reproduction, or lifespan.

gaps: The study addresses one adult social vocal behavior; development, reproduction, survival, and lifespan were not assessed.

claims.text: The study examined male-to-male responses to familiar and unfamiliar conspecific alarm callers that signal leopard or eagle stimuli. Its site-specific playback results support a bounded observation about social signaling and predator-associated alarm contexts, not a population-wide measure of predation risk or a complete interaction network.
claims.locator: Abstract; Introduction; Material and methods > Subjects and playback stimuli, paragraph beginning ‘We tested different groups of Diana monkeys’; Results > Call-related parameters, paragraph beginning ‘To eagle alarm calls, responses showed frequency transitions’; Discussion
claims.placeTimeScope: Playback experiments with wild Diana monkeys at Taï Forest, Côte d’Ivoire (August to December 2013), and Tiwai Island, Sierra Leone (January to March 2014); conclusions are restricted to those studied populations and experimental stimuli.
claims.lifeStatus: Wild male callers and receivers in the study populations; no captive or domesticated animals are included.

gaps: Two experimental study populations and selected leopard/eagle playback stimuli do not establish a complete interaction network, natural predation rates, range-wide ecology, or seasonality.
No phylogenetic placement, trait evolution, or divergence-time evidence was assessed.
Two study locations are not a range-wide inventory and do not establish native-range boundaries or change through time.
No fossil or paleontological search was performed; no fossil-presence or fossil-absence conclusion is made.
No current formal conservation assessment, status, trend, or population-risk analysis was reviewed.

reasons: Only bounded behavioral and social-signaling findings from one two-population playback study were assessed; five facets remain not-assessed and the two assessed facets are partial.
The study concerns C. diana diana and does not by itself establish full biological circumscription for the COL accepted species usage.
No comprehensive multi-source search or independent expert review has been completed.
